answerable: Sensitivity of surface runoff vs. deep drainage (recharge) partitioning to soil clay fraction under fixed forcing
Relative change in infiltration capacity and subsurface drainage across a clay gradient
Changes in soil moisture storage and evapotranspiration co-varying with clay content
not_answerable: Absolute recharge validation against site observations (no observational data provided)
Spatially distributed lateral runoff routing (single-column has no lateral connectivity)
Effects of clay mineralogy or macropore/preferential flow (not represented in default ELM hydrology)

parsed.n_justification: A controlled one-factor-at-a-time sweep of clay content across the requested 5%-55% range. Six columns at ~10% increments (5,15,25,35,45,55) sample the gradient with enough resolution to resolve the nonlinear runoff/recharge response while sharing identical location, forcing, and all other parameters so clay is the sole varied factor.
assumptions: All columns share identical atmospheric forcing (GSWP3/CLMNCEP 1980-2018), PFT, topography (fixed slope/fmax), and organic matter to isolate clay as the sole varied driver

Sand and silt fractions are adjusted to keep totals at 100% while holding sand roughly complementary; texture-derived van Genuchten/Clapp-Hornberger parameters are computed internally by ELM pedotransfer functions
A multi-year spin-up (first several years treated as equilibration) precedes analysis to remove initial soil moisture memory
Recharge is approximated by the sum of gravitational bottom drainage (QDRAI) and aquifer recharge (QCHARGE); runoff is QRUNOFF (QOVER + QDRAI baseflow separated in post-processing)
Default ELM hydrology (no macropore/preferential flow); results reflect matrix-flow partitioning only
Single-column configuration implies no lateral routing; QRGWL captures glacier/wetland/lake runoff terms assumed negligible here
